heroHeadline: IRGC Strikes Kuwait Airport — 1 Killed After US Hits Qeshm; Hezbollah Rejects Lebanon Ceasefire; IDF Capt. Lemberg ATGM Killed; Trump Reveals Rejected 'Nuclear Dust' Plan, Offers 20-Year Moratorium; MOU Unsigned — Day 98
heroSubtitle: Day 98 (June 5, 2026): The US-Iran 60-day MOU framework remains unsigned as Day 98 begins, with Brent crude stabilizing at approximately $95.25/bbl. On Day 96 (June 3), the US conducted airstrikes against IRGC drone control stations on Qeshm Island — the first confirmed US strike on Iranian-held territory since May 5. The IRGC retaliated the same day, launching 13 ballistic missiles and 17 drones at Kuwait; two missiles struck Kuwait International Airport, killing one Indian national and injuring 63+ others while damaging the passenger terminal. Three IRGC missiles targeting the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Manama, Bahrain were intercepted. CENTCOM called the Kuwait airport attack 'deliberate, calculated and unjustified.' Israel and Lebanon simultaneously agreed to ceasefire 'pilot zones' on June 3, but Hezbollah formally rejected the deal on June 4 (Day 97), calling negotiations 'absurd, humiliating and insulting.' In Lebanon, IDF Captain Eitan Shmuel Lemberg, 21 (7th Armored Brigade, 75th Battalion), was killed by a Hezbollah anti-tank guided missile (ATGM) fired at an Israeli tank north of the Litani River — the first Israeli soldier killed since the renewed ceasefire went into effect that morning. Israeli strikes killed four Lebanese on June 4. Iran declared 'no tangible progress' in US-Iran negotiations. Trump made his most significant diplomatic disclosures yet: he revealed publicly that he had rejected a US military plan to physically collect Iran's enriched uranium ('nuclear dust'), said he would accept Iran suspending nuclear enrichment for 20 years if there is a 'real commitment,' and signaled openness to a direct summit with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. The IRGC is charging transit fees exceeding $1 million per vessel for Hormuz passage, with approximately 15 ships per day authorized — compared to the pre-crisis baseline of 95 ships per day. Iran's core precondition — Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon — remains unmet and is the central obstacle to the MOU framework's signature on Day 98.
